title: Potential Field Path Planning Exercise
html:
Implement the Potential Field Path Planning algorithm. The robot is represented as a point that is attracted to the goal by an attractive potential and repelled from obstacles by a repulsive potential. The task is to guide the robot from the start to the goal while avoiding obstacles by following the combined potential field.

Problem Breakdown:

The attractive potential pulls the robot toward the goal.

The repulsive potential pushes the robot away from obstacles.

The total potential is the sum of both potentials: U(q)=Uatt(q)+Urep(q)U(q) = U_{att}(q) + U_{rep}(q)U(q)=Uatt​(q)+Urep​(q) Where:

Uatt(q)U_{att}(q)Uatt​(q) is the attractive potential at point qqq.

Urep(q)U_{rep}(q)Urep​(q) is the repulsive potential at point qqq.

Here is the visual representation of the grid:

Explanation:

S (0, 0) is the starting position.

G (8, 8) is the goal position.

The X symbols at coordinates (3, 3), (5, 5), and (7, 2) represent obstacles the robot must avoid.

Objective:

Your objective is to implement the Potential Field Path Planning algorithm to move the robot from S to G while avoiding obstacles at X. The robot should always follow the direction of the combined attractive and repulsive potential fields at each point.
